# their_thing: # "Theirs" is scikit-learn 1.9.1, the semantics reference for the prep lane's preprocessing, imputation and feature-selection classes (python/mojolearn/_expansion_prep.py). Every row is refused by name at the API. Option parity (docs/lanes/ALGORITHM_EXPANSION_PLAN.md, CURRENT DIRECTIVES item 2) works down this file.
sklearn OneHotEncoder / KBinsDiscretizer / LabelBinarizer / MultiLabelBinarizer sparse output
why / where it would go: there is no sparse Array; output is dense float32 (OneHotEncoder ignores sparse_output and says so in its docstring)

# their_thing: sklearn RFE ties between equal importances
why / where it would go: the reference ranks with np.argsort's default kind, an unstable introsort (a SIMD sort on some CPUs), so which of two equal importances is dropped first is unspecified and can differ by machine; mojolearn's order is a stable ascending sort (the lower column index is dropped first) on every column

# their_thing: sklearn OrdinalEncoder / OneHotEncoder inverse_transform None for an unknown row
why / where it would go: the reference returns an object array with None; there is no object Array, so the row's value is NaN

# their_thing: sklearn TargetEncoder training value outside categories=<list>
why / where it would go: the reference codes such a row as the FIRST category (`Xi[~valid_mask] = categories_[i][0]` in `_transform`) and so counts its target in that category's encoding; mojolearn leaves it out of every category's statistics (it still counts in the target mean)
the reference writes the string 'infrequent_sklearn' in an object array; there is no object Array, so the value is NaN

# their_thing: sklearn OrdinalEncoder unknown_value equal to the infrequent code
why / where it would go: the reference's collision check subtracts the infrequent categories from the cardinality without adding back their one grouped code, so unknown_value may equal it; mojolearn refuses that value like any other used code

# their_thing: sklearn KBinsDiscretizer quantile edges at an exact order-statistic position
why / where it would go: numpy computes the virtual index n * q - 1 with q = linspace(0, 100, nb + 1) / 100 cast to the data's float32, so a level whose exact position n * i / nb is an integer can land a rounding step off it and pick the neighbouring order statistic; mojolearn uses the exact rational position i / nb (integer arithmetic), the same on every column

# their_thing: sklearn SplineTransformer extrapolation='linear' with degree <= 1 and more than one feature
why / where it would go: the reference raises its local `degree` to 2 inside the per-feature loop and never resets it, so every feature after the first takes xmin, xmax = t[2], t[-3] and extrapolates rows inside its base interval; mojolearn uses each feature's own base interval (the first feature's reference output)

the reference assigns f_max[-0:] (every column) into zero columns and raises a shape mismatch for any x above xmax; mojolearn writes the reference's rule as stated, the last 0 columns, so such a row encodes as zeros

a weighted mean and weighted centred variance per column; the binding's standard_fit has no weight input. Keep the unweighted fit's bits: a new entry point (or x_prep units), not a change to standard_fit

the reference's `_incremental_mean_and_var` (Chan's update of the running sum and unnormalised variance) and the running min / max; the first batch must equal fit's bits (fit == partial_fit on a fresh scaler, as the reference)

# their_thing: sklearn StandardScaler / MinMaxScaler NaN (fit ignores NaN, per-feature n_samples_seen_; transform passes NaN through)
why / where it would go: `_input` refuses non-finite values; x_prep col_stats already folds over the non-NaN entries
the transform writes a new Array; in place means writing into the caller's float32 C-contiguous buffer
